subject: ACME RAG eval - post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hale <jordan.hale@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME RAG eval - post-call recap & next steps

Thanks again for taking the call today - great to meet the ACME team. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary of needs (what I heard)
- Use case: customer support knowledge base search + generative answer summarization for SLO'd responses to support tickets.
- Data: ~2.5M docs (guides, KB articles, transcripts); mix of short FAQs and long how-tos; strong importance on factual grounding and low hallucination.
- Success metrics: grounding rate (source citation present and correct) > 95% for top-1, end-to-end answer NDCG for retrieval+rerank, and mean token latency < 250ms on median for short queries.
- Constraints: prefer hybrid retrieval (dense + BM25) if we can keep cost within committed budget; enterprise security (VPC + KMS) required.

Redwood recommendations (initial)
1) Retriever: hybrid dense retriever (Faiss HNSW) + BM25 fallback. Use a retriever that returns top-100 shards then rerank.
2) Reranker: lightweight cross-encoder (distil-cross-encoder-xxl) for top-10 reordering - gives best tradeoff for grounding precision. We presented two candidate rerankers in the call; I recommend Reranker B (higher precision, slightly higher latency) for critical user flows, and Reranker A for lower-cost dashboards.
3) Generator/model: for grounded generation we recommend a medium-size instruction-tuned open model (redwood-icl-2.7b) as default; for higher-fidelity summarization we can test redwood-7b-rl or a 13b tuned variant.
4) Prompting: we attached the initial prompt set (acme_rag_promptset_v1.json). These include grounding instructions, citation format, and fallbacks for ambiguous queries.
5) Evaluation & metrics: we propose running a 1k-query eval set (mix of short/long and adversarial queries). Key metrics: grounding rate, source precision@1, reranker NDCG@5, ROUGE-L/QA-F1 vs labeled answers, and generation latency distribution.

Next steps
- We'll run a small pilot eval (1k queries) with our recommended config (hybrid retriever + Reranker B + redwood-icl-2.7b) and share the results in ~4 business days.
- Can you share an export of ~1k representative queries and a small document subset (we'll use redaction for PII)? A Drive link works.
- Tentative follow-up: Tue May 25 10am PT for review.

Attachments: acme_rag_promptset_v1.json, redwood-reranker-benchmarks.pdf

Thanks - I'll loop Rishi and Neha on the pilot design.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa - super helpful summary. A few clarifying Qs before we share the query sample: 
1) For the hybrid retriever, are you recommending sequential retrieval (dense then BM25) or fused scoring? Which achieves better recall on longer how-to docs?
2) For Reranker B - do you have benchmark numbers (precision@1, latency at 95th) on our doc-size profile? The benchmark PDF was helpful but wanted ACME-specific numbers if possible.
3) On model choices: we're worried about token costs at scale. If we start with redwood-icl-2.7b for generation, is there a recommended quantization profile we should expect to keep cost reasonable while preserving grounding quality?

We can have the dataset ready by EOD tomorrow. Tue May 25 10am PT works for Priya and me.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: ACME RAG eval - post-call recap & next steps

Hi all - quick pilot proposal (high-level numbers are approximate; will run a micro-benchmark against the sample you provide):

Pilot config (recommended) - Retriever: hybrid pipeline - dense retriever (Faiss HNSW, 768-d embeddings, top-500) fused with BM25 candidate scoring. We do dense embedding search first to get nearest neighbors, then merge BM25 hits and dedupe, then rerank. This gives better recall on long documents vs pure BM25 in our tests.
- Reranker: distil-cross-encoder-xxl ("Reranker B") - expected precision@1 ~0.88 on long-doc synthetic sample; NDCG@5 ~0.76. Med latency for rerank top-50 ~45ms (GPU); 95th ~120ms.
- Generator: redwood-icl-2.7b quantized to 4-bit (Q4_0) for pilot; quality regression observed vs fp16 is negligible on our prompt sets for grounding tasks, but we should validate on your labeled queries. If you care about the absolute best quality for summarization, test redwood-7b-rl in fp16.

Estimated perf/cost (ballpark per 1k queries, pilot config)
- Retrieval (dense + BM25 merge): ~1.2 CPU/GPU-minutes per 1k queries; retrieval infra cost ~ $8–12 per 1k.
- Rerank (top-50 x cross-encoder): ~0.9 GPU-minutes per 1k; cost ~ $20–30 per 1k depending on GPU type.
- Generation (2.7b Q4): ~0.5 GPU-minutes per 1k; cost ~ $6–10 per 1k.
Total pilot compute cost estimate: ~$35–50 per 1k queries (varies by instance and batching).

Next steps for us
1) If ACME can share the 1k query sample + a 10k-doc subset (redacted), we'll run the pilot in our sandbox and return benchmark artifacts and a short analysis (grounding rate + reranker lift) within 4 business days.
2) We'll include a comparison run with Reranker A (for cost tradeoffs) and one run using redwood-7b-rl on a 200-query subset to validate quality delta.

Attachments: small synthetic recall sample (internal).

Happy to sync Tue 10am PT for results.

Thanks,
Rishi
